subject: Post-call scoping: integration matrix, SDK/auth, and routing policy proposal
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alice Nguyen <alice@integral.tech>
Date: 2026-09-13T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap + asks — Integral Tech integration scope

Hi team / Alice,

Thanks again for the 60m today — we covered their primary use case (real-time conversational assistant inside their product + an internal re-ranker for search relevance). Quick recap and asks so we can scope a short POC: 

Summary (top-level)
- Integral wants a hosted API with a private VPC outbound (no long-term data residency requirement, US-first) and sub-200ms p50 generative latency for single-turn assistants.
- They will call for both structured tool-calling outputs (JSON with action tokens) and embeddings-based re-ranking (~512-d vectors).
- Expected peak concurrency: ~120 qps during business hours; average 25 qps.
- Budget range indicated in call: $25k–$40k / mo for pilot (covers modest throughput + eval period).

Immediate asks for engineering triage:
1) SDK + auth pattern: Alice prefers server-side service account flow + short-lived tokens for browserless clients. Need a recommended auth flow and example SDK snippets (Node + Python).
2) Routing policy: prefer latency-first for assistant routes, cost-sensitive for background rerankers. Need a proposed fallback chain (e.g., fast distilled model -> standard -> queued fallback) and region routing (US east primary, US west failover).
3) Structured outputs/tool calling: confirm how we enforce schema + a safety/confidence threshold to trigger external tool calls.
4) Embeddings/re-ranker: guidance on vector dimensionality, batching recommendations, and whether to use on-disk ANN versus managed Redis vector DB for pilot.

I attached the postcall notes and a rough YAML stub for a routing policy. Can the eng triage call out items that block starting a week-long POC?

Next steps (proposed)
- Dev: produce a 1-page SDK/auth recommendation + code snippets by Tue 9/15.
- Ben: follow up on procurement and get a statement of intent / PO timeline from Integral.
- Marissa: confirm sales terms to align with the $25k–$40k pilot band and whether we can include a trial discount.
- Alice/Bob: confirm target date to start POC (they suggested week of 9/22).

Thanks — Neha

--
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
neha@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alice Nguyen <alice@integral.tech>
Date: 2026-09-13T17:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + asks — Integral Tech integration scope

Thanks for the clear recap, Neha — calling out a few technical constraints and proposals so we can be concrete for the POC scope. I pulled the attached: sdk-auth-checklist.md (quick wins) and a starter routing-policy.yaml.

SDK / Auth
- Recommendation: server-to-server service account tokens minted via our private control plane (short-lived JWTs, 15m). Browser-origin calls should use a lightweight proxy to avoid exposing keys.
- Node + Python snippet: use SDK v2.1 (we introduced auto-retry headers to better surface transient GPU queueing).
- Blocking items: Integral must confirm which outbound IP ranges their infra allows for a VPC peering + whether they require a customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest.

Routing policy (proposal)
- Assistant route: latency-first policy: prefer model-r1-small (4-bit quant) for sub-150ms p50 at short sequences, fallback to model-r1-medium, final fallback -> queue to dedicated capacity with best-effort responses.
- Reranker route: cost-first policy: batch embeddings (up to 64) and route to quantized reranker model; if high latency detected (>500ms p95) route to async re-rank job with cached results.
- Region rule: primary us-east1, prefer us-west1 for users west of the Rockies; cross-region failover only for degraded capacity conditions (not normal).

Structured output/tool calling
- Use structured response schema enforcement at the model selector level (we can validate and drop requests that fail schema at inference time).
- Add an action confidence threshold (>=0.85) to trigger external tool calls; below threshold, return a clarification prompt to the user.

Embeddings & re-ranker
- Use 512 dims (default) for pilot; recommend batched generation with 32–64 batch size for throughput. Managed vector DB (Redis Vector or Pinecone) is simpler for POC; for production, we can propose beyond-SSD ANN (faiss-hnsw on dedicated infra) if they want lower latency.

Blockers for POC start
- Integral to confirm VPC peering window and KMS requirement.
- Integral to confirm data retention / logging sensitivity — if they need full audit logs we may need Private deployment licensing.

I'll prepare code snippets (Node/Python) and a short demo harness for the assistant flow by EOD Monday.

Cheers,
Dev

--
Dev Patel

dev_patel@redwood.ai

Subject: Fwd: Post-call recap + asks — integration plan and next steps

Alice / Bob — forwarding the engineering recommendations from Dev so you have a compact version for your infra team. Key asks for you to confirm:
1) VPC peering window (dates/times) and whether you require customer KMS.
2) Do you want the assistant latency SLO to target p50<150ms or p50<200ms? That affects model choice and pilot pricing.
3) For embeddings: ok to start with managed Redis Vector for POC?

If you can reply with quick answers to the three bullets we can lock a POC kickoff for week of 9/22 and ship SDK snippets on 9/15 as planned.

Thanks,
Neha

Date: 2026-09-14T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-call recap + asks — integration plan and next steps

Thanks Neha + Dev — short answers from our infra/product side: 
- VPC peering: we can open a window 9/23–9/24 for initial testing; prod peering will need a formal change request (we'll provide IP allowlist).
- KMS: for the pilot we can use Redwood-managed KMS, but production will need our KMS (we'll follow your KMS integration guide).
- Latency SLO: let's aim for p50<200ms for pilot (helps keep pilot cost in budget), but we'd like a path to p50<150ms for GA.
- Embeddings: managed Redis Vector is fine for pilot. We'll plan a short procurement path (PO in progress) and share a procurement doc link when ready.

We'll confirm the PO timeline by 9/17. If everything looks good we'll lock 9/23 as a tech kickoff.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Alice
Product Lead, Integral Tech
alice@integral.tech
